name: Shami Kebab
subtitle: dense little mutton and chana dal patties, smooth inside and crisp at the edge

ingredients.note: the binder. Nothing else does the same job

ingredients.qty: 1 medium quartered for the boil, 1 small very finely chopped for the mix

ingredients.note: helps the patties hold when frying
neutral oil works but tastes flatter

prepNotes: Soak the chana dal 1 hour in warm water. Undersoaked dal stays gritty and the kebab will crumble.
The cooked mince must be bone dry before grinding. Any moisture and the patties fall apart in the pan.
Chill the shaped kebabs 30 minutes before frying. They firm up and turn far more easily.

steps.text: Pressure cook the mutton, drained dal, quartered onion, garlic, ginger, whole chillies, black cardamom, green cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, peppercorns, salt and 250ml water for 5 whistles, about 20 minutes.
steps.tip: In a pan instead, allow 50 minutes covered on low.

steps.text: Open the lid and boil hard, stirring, until every trace of liquid has gone and the mix looks dry and sandy, 8–10 minutes.
steps.tip: This is the step people skip. Wet mince equals kebabs that disintegrate.

steps.text: Cool completely, then pick out the cinnamon stick and black cardamom shell and grind the rest to a smooth, tight paste with no added water.
Knead in the finely chopped onion, green chilli, coriander, mint, garam masala and the beaten egg. Taste for salt now.
Divide into 12 and shape into flat discs 5cm across and 1.5cm thick. Refrigerate 30 minutes.
Heat 2 tbsp ghee on a tawa over medium heat and lay in the kebabs without crowding.
Fry 3–4 minutes a side until a deep brown crust forms, adding the remaining ghee as you turn.
steps.tip: Turn once only, with a thin spatula. Fiddling breaks them.

steps.text: Drain on paper, rest 2 minutes and serve hot with lemon wedges and sliced onion.

storage: Cooked kebabs keep 3 days refrigerated and reheat well on a dry tawa over low heat. The raw ground mix freezes for a month; thaw fully before shaping.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
nutrition.caveat: Ingredients given to taste rather than by weight are counted as zero, so the real figure is a little higher than this. The + says so.
